column5: Look: a company command post at night. A dark map board with MIL-STD-2525 frames (blue rectangle friendly, red diamond hostile, yellow unknown), grease-pencil control measures, report marks that fade and dash with age, last-known-position ghosts with a time label, uncertainty ellipses. Beside it the radio and duty log in standard report formats, a platoon status board, and the intelligence cell's target file. Orange only for "a decision is waiting on you". Every figure drawn as a symbol, no emoji, no plain circles. *(inferred (strong))*
References: Command: Modern Operations (fog, sensor-driven picture); Football Manager (indirect control, people you come to know). *(inferred (strong))*
View: 2D · Camera: top-down map board with pan and zoom. *(provisional)*
The village: about 20 families in compounds, each with routines and a hidden leaning with recorded causes
The cell: the leader, a handful of fighters, a cache, rooftop spotters, taxing the road, intimidating informants, acting only on what it has seen or been told
Your company: three platoons with soldiers, fatigue and a rotation (outpost security, available, resting)
Tasking by mission, intent and limits, with the platoon leader's back-brief to approve or return: presence patrol, compound search, meeting with an elder, raid
Reports from the field: delayed and partial spot reports, debriefs on return, tips from families who lean your way
The command post: map board updated only from reports, radio and duty log, status board, target file
Standing reporting requirements and time acceleration that the staff interrupt
Debrief at the end: what your side learned, and when

The ops room at 1800.
The duty log shows battalion's order: capture the cell leader, call sign unknown, believed in the village, within 48 hours.
The map board shows your outpost, the village compounds and the road; the status board shows three platoons, one on outpost security.
The executive officer's note suggests a presence patrol and a meeting with the village elder.
You task 2nd Platoon: mission, intent, limits.
A few minutes of game time later the platoon leader back-briefs his route, timing and actions on contact; you approve.
On the map, the platoon symbol moves only as its position reports come in.
An hour later a spot report arrives, and the first marks appear on the board.
*(guessed)*
Within the first few in-game hours, a spotter on a rooftop reports your patrol to the cell, so the leader avoids where you are.
A heavy-handed search or a civilian casualty turns families against you, drying up tips.
Tired platoons make mistakes.
He escapes if spooked into leaving the area or when 48 hours run out; the session ends with a debrief built only from what your side learned.
Later sessions grow the area and the deadline.
*(provisional)*
